title: Accelerating Zero-Knowledge Proofs Through Hardware-Algorithm Co-Design
problem: Zero-Knowledge Proof generation has prohibitive costs that limit applications to simple computations. Prior ZKP accelerators are not designed to exploit the parallelism and efficiency opportunities in hash-based ZKP algorithms.
motivation: Zero-Knowledge Proofs enable cryptographic correctness guarantees for applications like verifiable ML, databases, blockchains, and auctions, but proof generation costs currently limit practical deployment.
method: NoCap combines hash-based ZKP algorithms (Orion and Spartan) with a specialized programmable vector processor featuring custom functional units tailored to ZKP operations. The co-designed implementation optimizes for parallelism and reduces memory traffic through algorithm-specific hardware organization while accepting larger proof sizes for end-to-end speedup.
key_novelty: Hardware-algorithm co-design that leverages hash-based ZKP algorithms (Orion and Spartan) amenable to hardware acceleration with a specialized vector processor architecture featuring application-specific functional units.
contributions: Programmable vector processor architecture with custom functional units tailored to hash-based ZKPs
Identification and combination of Orion and Spartan algorithms optimized for hardware acceleration
Co-designed hardware-software implementation with optimizations for parallelism and memory traffic reduction
586× speedup over 32-core CPU and 41× speedup over PipeZK accelerator
limitations: Hash-based algorithms produce larger proofs than prior ZKP approaches, though end-to-end speedups including prover time, transmission, and verification justify the tradeoff.
